validated_work_order.understanding:
v2 was rejected on one count, confined to the QA-facing text: AC-3's how_to_verify and qa_script step 7 told QA to read date filter chips labelled 'is after or equals <From>' and 'is before or equals <end>', which the accounts page does not render. Re-derived from source rather than accepted: FilterExpression.tsx:87 renders `{friendlyOp(op, null)}` — it passes null as the type argument, not 'date'. util/rule.ts:109-113 (case 'gte') and :115-123 (case 'lte') gate the date wording on `type === 'date'`, so with null both fall through to t('is greater than or equals') / t('is less than or equals'). mapField('date', options) returns t('date') (util/rule.ts:56-57) and Value renders the date itself for field 'date' (Value.tsx:101-107, reached because subfieldFromFilter returns 'date' for a 10-char yyyy-MM-dd value). The chips therefore read 'date is greater than or equals <date>' and 'date is less than or equals <date>'. v2's evidence bullet cited FilterExpression.tsx:81-95 and util/rule.ts:108-121 as confirming the label, but those ranges contain the friendlyOp cases and not the `null` argument at the call site, which is what decides the branch.

The criterion's substance is sound and is unchanged. showActivity.ts:80-95 builds the gte/lte pair for both drilldown paths — the BarGraph totals bar (type 'totals', interval not passed so 'Day' defaults, so isDateOp = interval === 'Weekly' || type !== 'time' is true) and the Data Table totals cell (ReportTableRow.tsx:311-330, same type). Both read data.endDate (BarGraph.tsx:340-341, ReportTable.tsx:88-89/:115-116 passed to ReportTableRow.tsx:321-322), so once setData carries the widened date both carry it. Only the quoted label was wrong.

The code plan is unchanged from v2 and was not objected to. Findings 1, 4 and 5 are one defect: the Weekly end-date rule exists in three copies — custom-spreadsheet.ts:125-128, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:58-61, recalculate.ts:90-108 (confirmed by grep: those three plus reportRanges.ts:196 in getSpecificRange, an unrelated preset, are the only getWeekEnd callers under desktop-client/src) — and never reached the two places a human reads a date: the summary header (CustomReport.tsx:1074 passes raw endDate from useState at :268-269) and setData (custom-spreadsheet.ts:342). Finding 5 is the inconsistency inside that rule: the widening is unconditional while the remapping twelve lines below is guarded with balanceTypeOp !== 'totalBudgeted' (custom-spreadsheet.ts:147, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:80), and fetchBudgetData keys rows by month. Finding 2 is a one-word release-note fix. Finding 3 is not fixable here. Findings 6 and 7 are pre-existing a11y errors — both re-confirmed still standing by reading (CommandBar.tsx:269-291, ReportCard.tsx:108-127).
validated_work_order.root_cause: The Weekly end-date rule is implemented inline in three separate places — custom-spreadsheet.ts:125-128, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:58-61 and recalculate.ts:90-108 — with a fourth consumer at custom-spreadsheet.ts:266. Because there is no single home for the rule, the two consumers that render a date to the user were never given it: ReportSummary is passed the raw endDate from CustomReport.tsx:1074, and setData passes the raw endDate into DataEntity at custom-spreadsheet.ts:342. The header therefore reports the week start while the bucket beneath it runs to the week's true last day. The same triplication is why the rule's own internal guard (balanceTypeOp !== 'totalBudgeted', honoured by the date remapping at :147 and :80) is absent from the widening, so the budgeted path is widened while being deliberately excluded from the remap that makes Weekly buckets match.
validated_work_order.approach:
Extract the Weekly end-date rule into one exported getEffectiveEndDate in reportRanges.ts, next to the other range-normalisation helpers, and route all four existing sites plus the two leaky consumers through it. One helper rather than four patches, because the drift between copies is what produced the header bug.

The helper takes balanceTypeOp as well as interval, so the budgeted exclusion lives in the same statement as the widening instead of one clause of the rule being applied and another skipped.

Three of the four sites already compute the value correctly and already call it effectiveEndDate; they only change shape. recalculate.ts changes its input from intervalItem to endDate, which is behaviour-identical because the last element of weekRangeInclusive(startDate, endDate) is weekFromDate(endDate) (months.ts:292-319) and getWeekEnd is idempotent within a week (it is d.endOfWeek, months.ts:401-409).

Then close the two consumers the rule never reached: custom-spreadsheet.ts:342 passes endDate: effectiveEndDate into setData, and CustomReport.tsx:1074 passes data.endDate to ReportSummary instead of its own raw endDate state. That single setData change makes the header, the totals bar drilldown and the totals row drilldown all agree with the data beneath them, without touching any of those four files.

Tests: the helper gets pure unit tests in reportRanges.test.ts covering pass-through, widening, clamp, Monday first-day and budgeted. custom-spreadsheet.test.ts gains assertions that data.endDate matches the final bucket's intervalEndDate. Existing expectations are not touched — they prove the move was behaviour-preserving, so a diff there means the extraction changed something it should not have.

What changed from v2 is confined to AC-3's how_to_verify and qa_script step 7: both now name the labels the accounts page actually renders and identify the target chip positionally as well.

acceptance.check: A Weekly custom report whose To date is a week start shows a summary header ending on that week's true last day, or on today while the week is still in progress. The header never shows the To date itself for a Weekly report whose week has more than one day left in it.

Read the header's end date as text. Pick a To date that is a week start at least one full week in the past, so its week has certainly elapsed whatever day QA runs; the header's end date must be the last day of that week (the To date plus six days) and must not be the To date. Then pick the current week's start; the header's end date must be today's date and never later. Do not compare against a bucket date range — no component in the reports view renders one (see out_of_scope); AC-3 covers where the range is visible.

qa_script: yarn start, and on the welcome screen choose 'Try the demo' (WelcomeScreen.tsx:130) so the budget has transactions.
Use a window wider than 512px. The summary header is not rendered at narrow widths (CustomReport.tsx:1063), and the report's totals row is not clickable there either (ReportTableRow.tsx:83-84).
Go to Reports, open a custom report, set Interval to Weekly, and click the calculator icon ('Show Summary') in the topbar so the header is visible.

Note today's date. Note the start of the current week under the current first-day-of-week setting (Sunday-first by default). Set From to a week start four or five weeks earlier and To to exactly one week before the current week's start — a week start whose week has therefore already fully elapsed, on any run date. (The To pickers only offer week starts: allIntervals is built with weekRangeInclusive at CustomReport.tsx:376-380.)

Assert the header's end date is the last day of the week whose start is the To date you picked — the To date plus six days — and that it is NOT the To date. Worked example: today is Friday 2026-10-02, first day of week is Sunday, current week starts 2026-09-27, so To is 2026-09-20 and the header must end 2026-09-26 (Saturday). The assertion above it is the rule; the example illustrates it.

Set To to the start of the current week. Assert the header's end date is today's date, and is never a date later than today. Worked example: with the same today, To is 2026-09-27 and the header must end 2026-10-02 (Friday), not the week's Saturday 2026-10-03.

Click any bar in the Bar Graph (or the Totals cell of the totals row in the Data Table). The activity list opens on /accounts. Above the transaction table, find the two filter chips whose text begins with the word 'date' — there are exactly two, and the second is the upper bound. Their text as rendered is 'date is greater than or equals <From>' and 'date is less than or equals <end>'. Assert the second one shows the same final-week last day you asserted in step 5, not the To date you picked. Do not look for 'is after or equals' or 'is before or equals': FilterExpression.tsx:87 calls friendlyOp(op, null) without the 'date' type argument, so the accounts page renders the numeric-operator wording instead (util/rule.ts:109-123). A chip row may also contain the drilldown's category chip and an amount chip; ignore those.
Settings > Formatting: set first day of the week to Monday, then reload the report.

RE-PICK To to a Monday week start one week before the current Monday week start. You must pick it again — changing the first day of the week rebuilds the To options (the effect at CustomReport.tsx:417-465 calls onSetAllIntervals, which is where weekRangeInclusive at :376-380 applies the new week boundary) but does not re-snap the stored To date, and the old Sunday date is no longer a valid week start under Monday-first. Worked example: today is Friday 2026-10-02, so the current Monday week starts 2026-09-28, To is 2026-09-21, and the header must end 2026-09-27 (Sunday).
Switch Interval to Daily, Monthly and Yearly with Summary still on; for each, pick a To date from that interval's picker and assert the header's end date is exactly the date you picked.

Confirm the browser console logged no new errors or warnings from the reports screen during the above. (The command-palette DialogTitle warning and the nested-button warning on /reports are pre-existing and out of scope for this ticket — see out_of_scope.)
risks: Widening DataEntity.endDate also widens the drilldown ranges that read it — BarGraph.tsx:340-341, DonutGraph.tsx (same data.startDate/data.endDate pattern), ReportTable.tsx:88-89 and :115-116 (passed to ReportTableRow.tsx:226-227, :274-275, :321-322). Those drilldowns currently open a window shorter than the totals they sit under, so this is a fix, but it is a behaviour change on several screens and must be stated in the PR description rather than discovered in review. The per-bucket cell drilldown (ReportTableRow.tsx:171-172) reads intervalItem.intervalStartDate/intervalEndDate and is unaffected.

recalculate.ts changes its last-bucket input from intervalItem to endDate. I believe these are always equal (the last element of weekRangeInclusive(startDate, endDate) is weekFromDate(endDate) — months.ts:292-319 — and getWeekEnd is idempotent within a week) but the existing tests only cover the Custom/Grouped paths, which both build intervals the same way. If an existing expectation in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts has to change to accommodate this, stop and re-derive rather than updating the expectation.

The budgeted exclusion is a behaviour change on the Weekly+Budgeted path, not just a tidy-up: today the query bound widens there and will no longer. No visible result changes, because budget rows are month-keyed and match no weekly bucket either way — but if some caller reaches Weekly+Budgeted with a non-month key (GetCardData.tsx:112-160 passes report.interval and the mapped balanceTypeOp through uncoerced, and ReportSidebar.tsx:199-206/:366-371 only coerces on user events, not at load), that caller would lose a month of budget rows it was previously fetching. The route to check first is the dashboard weekly widget.

GetCardData.tsx feeds the dashboard cards and calls the same two spreadsheet factories with raw report dates (lines 127-160), so its setData also gains the widened endDate and its BarGraph drilldowns widen with it. It does not render ReportSummary — it renders ChooseGraph (GetCardData.tsx:187-201) — and ReportSummary has exactly one caller in the tree (CustomReport.tsx:1072), so the header fix is scoped to the standalone report screen. The implementer should confirm this rather than assume it.

Adding balanceTypeOp to recalculateProps touches three call sites (custom-spreadsheet.ts:285, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:104 and :122). A missed one is a type error, not a silent bug, so typecheck will catch it.

Both release notes carry authors: [Shivam-Fl] on the precedent of PR #10's note. If the repo owner wants a different attribution, this is a one-word change in two files and should be corrected before merge rather than after.
out_of_scope: Finding 3 — PR #12's title is missing the [AI] prefix. Not fixable in this repository: gh pr view 12 reports state MERGED with author app/github-actions, so there is no file to change, and .github/** is on forbidden_paths in any case. Retroactively editing a merged PR's title is a repo-owner call about their own history, not a code change. The rule this PR does have to follow is its own title, which must start with [AI].

Finding 6 — the cmdk Command.Dialog in CommandBar.tsx:269-291 logs a missing-DialogTitle a11y warning on every Ctrl+K open: it passes label and aria-label but renders no DialogTitle child. Confirmed by reading the component; pre-existing, in the global command palette, with no relationship to report date ranges. Fixing it means either giving the dialog a visually-hidden title or upgrading cmdk — neither belongs in a report-range bugfix. Worth its own issue.

Finding 7 — /reports nests a <button> inside a <button>: ReportCard.tsx:108-127 wraps card content in a Button when `to && !isEditing && !disableClick`, and CalendarCard supplies `to` and renders a second bare Button for the month label. Also pre-existing and unrelated to date ranges, and the fix is a genuine design call rather than a mechanical one: removing the outer button changes the whole card's click behaviour, removing the inner one drops keyboard access to that month's link. Someone who knows the intended interaction needs to pick.

Making Weekly+Budgeted impossible rather than merely inert. The sidebar already disables Daily/Weekly when Budgeted is selected, but that is an event handler, not load-time normalisation, so a saved report with interval Weekly and balanceTypeOp Budgeted still reaches this code. Coercing at load time in GetCardData.tsx would be the real fix; it changes what a saved report renders, which is a product decision beyond this ticket.

Rendering a bucket's date range anywhere in the reports view. v1's AC-1 asked QA to compare the header against 'the final bucket's date range'; that comparison is not performable because ReportTableHeader renders only header.date (the interval start) per column and the stacked bar renders only {label}, the bucket's start. Every intervalStartDate/intervalEndDate read in packages/desktop-client/src sits inside an onClick drilldown payload, never in displayed text. Adding a range label to the graph or table would be a new feature with its own design decision (which format, where it sits, what it does at narrow widths), so this change points QA at the accounts-page filter chips instead — where the range genuinely is rendered.

'gte' : 'is', value: isDateOp ? startDate : monthUtils[fromDate](startDate), type: 'date'}` and `{field: 'date', op: 'lte', value: endDate, options: {date: true}}`. isDateOp = interval === 'Weekly' || type !== 'time' (showActivity.ts:55) evaluates true for both drilldown paths: the BarGraph totals bar passes type 'totals' and no interval, so interval defaults to 'Day' (showActivity.ts:41); the Data Table totals cell also passes type 'totals' (ReportTableRow.tsx:311-330). Finding 4 (rule triplicated): confirmed at three sites with identical bodies — custom-spreadsheet.ts:125-128, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:58-61, recalculate.ts:90-108 — plus the fourth consumer at custom-spreadsheet.ts:266. grep for getWeekEnd across packages/desktop-client/src and packages/loot-core/src returns exactly these three call sites plus reportRanges.ts:196 (inside getSpecificRange, an unrelated date-preset helper) plus the definition at months.ts:401. The only importers of recalculate are custom-spreadsheet.ts:285 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:104/122.

Finding 5 (unguarded widening): confirmed. The widening at custom-spreadsheet.ts:125-128 and grouped-spreadsheet.ts:58-61 has no balanceTypeOp condition, while the remapping immediately below it (custom-spreadsheet.ts:147, grouped-spreadsheet.ts:80) is guarded with balanceTypeOp !== 'totalBudgeted'. fetchSpreadsheetQueryData routes the budgeted case to fetchBudgetData, and budgetDataQuery.ts:210-213 does rangeInclusive(getMonth(startDate), getMonth(endDate)), so the guard is meaningful.

Finding 2 (release-note author): confirmed by reading the file — upcoming-release-notes/fix-weekly-report-final-bucket.md still reads authors: [claude], and packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:138 requires GitHub usernames. The precedent note fix-running-balance-ascending-sort.md reads authors: [Shivam-Fl].
Finding 3 (PR title): NOT fixable here. gh pr view 12 reports state MERGED, author app/github-actions. There is no file to edit, and .github/** is in forbidden_paths.

Findings 6 and 7 (a11y console errors): confirmed still present by tracing, not by running. CommandBar.tsx:269-291 renders Command.Dialog with label and aria-label and no Dialog.Title child. ReportCard.tsx:108-127 renders the outer Button when `to && !isEditing && !disableClick`, and CalendarCard supplies `to`. Both pre-existing and unrelated to this ticket's subject matter, so both are deferred.

Existing regression net: packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts (338 lines) already pins the Weekly widening across all three copies, including grouped-vs-custom equality, a Monday first-day case (startDate/endDate 2026-09-28, today pinned 2026-10-05, asserting both queryEndDates and the final intervalEndDate are 2026-10-04), and the Daily/Monthly pass-through. It pins currentDay with vi.spyOn via a pinToday helper (lines 50-52), which is the pattern reportRanges.test.ts will need. Those cases must survive the extraction unmodified.

Two surfaces QA needs, both confirmed by reading: the summary header is gated on !isNarrowWidth (CustomReport.tsx:1063) so a narrow window shows no header at all, and the Data Table's totals row only drills when !isNarrowWidth && groupBy !== 'Interval' && !compact (ReportTableRow.tsx:83-84), so the totals-cell path needs a wide window too. isNarrowWidth is width < breakpoints.small, and small is 512 (component-library/src/hooks/useResponsive.ts:15, tokens.ts:12). The default split is 'Category' (ReportOptions.ts:21), which satisfies the groupBy condition, and the demo entry point is 'Try the demo' (WelcomeScreen.tsx:130).

Limitation stated honestly: this checkout has no node_modules, so yarn test, yarn typecheck and a browser run were all unavailable to me. Every finding above was confirmed by reading code on main, and the Weekly end-date findings are additionally corroborated by the passing test suite already on main — but nothing here was reproduced by me in a live app.

alternatives_considered.approach: Patch each of the four sites in place (compute the clamped date in CustomReport, keep the three inline copies).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is four edits to preserve a bug class rather than remove it, and it leaves finding 4 unfixed — the drift between copies is exactly what let the header miss the rule in the first place.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix only the header, by computing the widened date inside ReportSummary from interval and firstDayOfWeekIdx.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The header is not the only consumer with the raw endDate — setData's endDate drives several drilldown surfaces, which is the same DataEntity ReportTable and the graphs read. A fifth copy of the rule in a presentation component would make the disagreement more likely, not less.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the helper interval-only (endDate, interval, firstDayOfWeekIdx) and add the balanceTypeOp !== 'totalBudgeted' guard at each call site.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That re-states the exclusion in two files, which is the duplication finding 4 is about. Passing balanceTypeOp into the helper puts the guard and the widening in one statement, and the cost is one extra prop on recalculate (already threaded from three call sites) rather than a repeated condition.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the objection by passing 'date' as the type argument at FilterExpression.tsx:87 so the accounts page renders the date wording v2 quoted.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would make AC-3's original wording true, but it changes a global filter chip's label for every user of every date filter — a cosmetic change to an unrelated component, in a bugfix about report date ranges, to satisfy a test script. Naming the label the code actually renders costs nothing and changes no behaviour.

alternatives_considered.approach: Identify the two date chips purely positionally ('the second chip above the transaction table') and drop the label wording entirely.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Rejected as the sole identification, not as part of it. The chip row is not guaranteed to contain only date filters — showActivity also emits a drilldown category chip and, for some balance types, an amount chip — so 'the second chip' is ambiguous where 'the second of the two chips beginning with the word date' is not. v3 gives both the corrected label and the positional form.

alternatives_considered.approach: Move the helper into a new file next to the spreadsheets rather than into reportRanges.ts.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: reportRanges.ts is already the report layer's home for range-normalisation rules and already imports monthUtils and SyncedPrefs; the helper needs no new plumbing and a new file would be one more place to look.

alternatives_considered.approach: Plan all seven findings in one work order, since the issue asks for all seven.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Findings 6 and 7 are pre-existing a11y defects in two unrelated subsystems, and finding 3 is not fixable in this repo. Bundling them would widen the diff and the review surface for a report-range bugfix without serving the ticket's actual complaint. Raised as a route_request instead so a human decides.

validated_work_order.debate_summary:
Council plan (v3). The v2 rejection had a single objection, and it is a QA-facing wording defect rather than a code defect, so the code plan carries over unchanged and this revision is confined to AC-3 and qa_script step 7. I re-derived the objection from the source rather than accepting it: FilterExpression.tsx:87 passes `null` as friendlyOp's type argument, so util/rule.ts:109-123 takes the numeric-operator branch and the chips read 'date is greater than or equals' / 'date is less than or equals'. That is confirmed, and v2's evidence bullet was wrong in the way the reviewer identified — it cited the friendlyOp cases but not the call site's `null`, which is what decides the branch. The reviewer's substance check also holds: showActivity builds the gte/lte pair for both drilldown paths and both read data.endDate, so the criterion is correct and only its wording was wrong.

Two judgement calls. First, I took the reviewer's primary suggestion — identify the chips positionally — but did not take it as the only identification: the chip row can also carry a drilldown category chip and an amount chip, so 'the second chip' alone is ambiguous. v3 gives both the corrected label and the positional form ('the second of the two chips beginning with the word date'), so QA can use either and the step survives a future rewording either way. Second, I rejected the alternative of fixing the label at the source — passing 'date' at FilterExpression.tsx:87 would make v2's original wording true, but it changes a global filter chip's label for every date filter in the app, a cosmetic change to an unrelated component made to satisfy a test script. Naming what the code renders costs nothing.

The v2 arithmetic fixes stand unchanged and were re-verified: getWeekEnd is endOfWeek with weekStartsOn, so a Monday To under Sunday-first returns itself; the To pickers only offer week starts; changing the first day of week rebuilds the option list without re-snapping the stored date; and the last element of weekRangeInclusive is weekFromDate(end), which is what makes recalculate's intervalItem -> endDate switch behaviour-identical. Scope is unchanged from v2: findings 1, 2, 4 and 5 are planned; 3, 6 and 7 are deferred with the scope_changed request to a maintainer.
residual_risks: If any existing expectation in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts must change to accommodate recalculate's intervalItem -> endDate switch, the extraction was not behaviour-preserving and the plan's central claim is wrong. The implementer should stop and re-derive rather than update the expectation.

The QA script's worked examples are written against today = 2026-10-02. They are illustrations of the rule, not the rule itself; the assertions above each one are stated as arithmetic (the To date plus six days; today's date) so they hold on whatever day QA runs. If a later revision finds QA treating a worked example as the expected literal, the script should be reworded to drop the examples entirely rather than re-dated.

The authors: [Shivam-Fl] attribution rests on the precedent of PR #10's note rather than on a decision recorded by the repo owner; if that precedent does not hold, both release notes need a one-word correction before merge.

Because node_modules is absent here, neither the typecheck nor the unit suite was executed against this plan before it was written. The pre-existing 338-line test suite makes a regression loud rather than silent, but the first `yarn test` in implement is still the first real verification of the refactor.

route_request.reason: This ticket is really two tickets. Findings 1, 4 and 5 are one defect — the Weekly end-date rule is triplicated and never reached the summary header or setData — and are planned here as a single helper-sized fix. Finding 3 (PR #12's title lacks [AI]) is not fixable in this repository: the PR is MERGED and .github/** is a forbidden path. Findings 6 and 7 are pre-existing a11y console errors in the command palette (cmdk Command.Dialog missing a DialogTitle, CommandBar.tsx:269-291) and the reports dashboard (ReportCard's Button wrapping CalendarCard's month-label Button), unrelated to report date ranges; finding 7's fix is a design call about which of the two buttons survives, not a mechanical edit. This plan therefore covers 1, 2, 4 and 5 and defers 3, 6 and 7 — a maintainer should decide whether to file 6 and 7 as separate issues rather than carry them through implement/review/qa on a report-range bugfix.
